name: Dragon dagger
description: Puncture, the dragon dagger's special attack: twenty-five per cent energy for two hits, each with fifteen per cent added accuracy and damage, rolled independently against the target's slash defence.

name: Abyssal dagger
description: Abyssal Puncture, the abyssal dagger's special attack: twenty-five per cent energy for two hits with twenty-five per cent added accuracy and fifteen per cent reduced damage, rolled against the target's slash defence. One accuracy roll decides both hits, so they land or miss together, which is why the shape is a shared roll rather than the dragon dagger's independent pair: the same expectation, a different distribution.

name: Granite hammer
description: Hammer Blow, the granite hammer's special attack: sixty per cent energy for one attack with fifty per cent added accuracy and five guaranteed extra damage, dealt even when the attack misses. The five is a shape rather than a damage factor because nothing scales it and it does not depend on the hit landing. The carve-out for NPCs immune to normal attacks needs no code, since immunity is resolved before the hit distribution runs. No defence style is stated for it, so the weapon's own crush roll applies.

quotes: which consumes 60% of the player's special attack energy, and deals an attack with 50% increased accuracy, while guaranteeing 5 additional damage to that attack
even if the special attack misses, the target will still take a minimum of 5 damage from it

name: Dragon mace
description: Shatter, the dragon mace's special attack: twenty-five per cent energy for one hit with twenty-five per cent added accuracy and fifty per cent added damage, rolled against the target's crush defence. The crush roll is declared explicitly rather than left to coincide with the mace's own attack style.

quotes: increases the player's accuracy by 25% and damage by 50%, while rolling against the target's crush defence

name: Dragon sword
description: Wild Stab, the dragon sword's special attack: forty per cent energy for one hit with twenty-five per cent added accuracy and damage, always rolled against the target's stab defence whatever style the sword is set to, which is why the defence style is a declared override. Its bypassing of Protect from Melee is a PvP prayer rule and has no place in an NPC damage model.

quotes: consumes 40% of the player's special attack energy to hit the target with 25% increased accuracy and damage

name: Dragon longsword

quotes: raises the player's maximum hit by 25% for one hit

name: Dragon scimitar

name: Abyssal bludgeon

There is no accuracy modifier and the special uses the bludgeon's ordinary crush roll.

quotes: increases damage dealt by 0.5% for every prayer point that the wielder is missing, consuming 50% of the wielder's special attack energy

name: Arclight

That drain lowers the opponent's Strength, Attack and Defence levels by 5% of base level plus 1, or 10% against demons, and stacks additively; it is the player-asserted state modelled by DefenceReductions.arclight rather than something this row prices.

name: Ancient godsword
description: Models the ancient godsword's Blood Sacrifice special attack: it costs 50% special attack energy, has doubled accuracy, and inflicts a 10% higher maximum hit than a normal attack. That 10% is the hidden godsword multiplier, so the row sets the godsword flag and carries no damage factor of its own. The delayed sacrifice is not modelled: on a landed hit the target is marked and eight ticks later takes 25 typeless damage unless it moves five tiles away, and whether it escapes is a positional question this engine has no model for, the damage is typeless so belongs to no part of the hit pipeline, and it lands eight ticks after the swing, which a steady-state per-attack model would have to amortise. Against a stationary boss this understates the special by up to 25 damage per cast.

quotes: In addition to doubled accuracy, it inflicts damage with a 10% higher maximum hit than a normal attack, consuming 50% of the player's special attack energy.

the target will be marked for sacrifice and will have eight ticks (4.8 seconds) to move at least five tiles away from the attacker. If the target fails to do so, they will take 25 typeless magic damage

name: Dragon halberd
description: Models the dragon halberd's Sweep special attack: it costs 30% special attack energy, gives a 10% damage boost, and rolls against the opponent's slash defence. Against monsters larger than 1x1 it lands a second hit with 25% reduced accuracy, which this engine reads as a reduced attack roll rather than a scaled hit chance, an assumption HalberdSweepSecondHit records as pinned rather than sourced. The multi-combat sweep across a 3x1 area is not modelled: that is a multi-target effect needing a target count, whereas the size-gated second hit is the single-target mechanic this row covers.

quotes: consuming 30% of the player's special attack energy. In addition to a 10% damage boost, if used against "large" monsters (anything that is larger than 1x1, such as most Boss monsters), the special attack will deal an additional second hit onto them, although with 25% reduced accuracy.

The minimum and the fang's double accuracy roll both stay, and OsmumtenFangMechanic owns both branches.

name: Dragon thrownaxe
description: Models the dragon thrownaxe's Momentum Throw special attack: it costs 25% special attack energy and improves accuracy by 25% with no damage modifier. It is the first ranged row and is self-contained, since thrownaxes need no ammunition. The instant flag is deliberately not set: the throw lands on the next tick but counts as a normal attack and resets the player's attack delay, so it consumes a full attack cycle like any other special, and the queue-jump it grants falls inside the perfect-switching idealisation the composition layer already assumes.
